title: Cofibrant resolutions of two-block simplicial collages
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, Dwyer--Kan equivalences and the Bergner model structure of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and the enriched projective model structures of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. A local trivial fibration is a simplicial functor inducing a trivial Kan fibration on each mapping simplicial set. Fix a universe containing all data. Let $U,V$ be disjoint small sets and let $D$ be a simplicial category on $U\amalg V$ with $D(v,u)=\varnothing$ for every $u\in U,v\in V$. Write $D_U,D_V$ for its full subcategories. Suppose $q_U:C_U\to D_U$ and $q_V:C_V\to D_V$ are local trivial fibrations, equal to the identity on their object sets, with $C_U,C_V$ Bergner cofibrant.

There exists a projectively cofibrant enriched functor $M:C_U^{\mathrm{op}}\times C_V\to\mathsf{sSet}$ and an objectwise trivial Kan fibration $M(u,v)\to D(u,v)$, where the target actions are restricted along $q_U,q_V$. Define $C$ to have these two diagonal categories, mapping sets $C(u,v)=M(u,v)$, reverse mapping sets $C(v,u)=\varnothing$, and composition given by the two commuting module actions. Then $C$ is Bergner cofibrant, both full inclusions $C_U\to C$ and $C_V\to C$ are Bergner cofibrations, and the resulting functor $C\to D$ fixing objects and extending $q_U,q_V$ is a local trivial fibration. For each $u\in U$, the covariant $C_V$-module $M(u,-)$ is projectively cofibrant; for each $v\in V$, the contravariant $C_U$-module $M(-,v)$ is projectively cofibrant. Choices may be made functorially for block-preserving simplicial functors together with compatible maps of the two prescribed diagonal resolutions; the object functions within blocks need not be injective. Empty blocks and empty mixed mapping sets are allowed, and no local Kan condition is required.

source.place: Appendix A.3.3, Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remark A.3.3.5 (projective model structures and free module cells), and Bergner math/0406507, Section 1 generators (C1),(C2), Section 2 Definition 2.1 (free maps): background for this agent-formulated collage construction lemma, not a quotation. Both read online; archival copies WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-enriched assertion.

proof.text: Put $I=C_U^{\mathrm{op}}\times C_V$, so that enriched functors $I\to\mathsf{sSet}$ are exactly simplicial sets $N(u,v)$ with commuting contravariant $C_U$- and covariant $C_V$-actions. Let $E(u,v)=D(u,v)$ with its actions restricted along $q_U,q_V$ (these are the identity on objects). By [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] (with $\mathcal A=\mathsf{sSet}$) projective fibrations and weak equivalences are objectwise, so the projective trivial fibrations are the objectwise trivial Kan fibrations, and evaluation at $i$ has left adjoint $X\mapsto I(i,-)\otimes X$. Let $\mathcal J$ be the small set of free cells $I(i,-)\otimes\partial\Delta^n\to I(i,-)\otimes\Delta^n$, $i\in\operatorname{Ob}I$, $n\geq0$. By this adjunction and the boundary characterization of trivial fibrations in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $\mathcal J^{\pitchfork}$ is exactly the class of objectwise trivial Kan fibrations. Construct $M$ by the countable small-object iteration: $M_0=\varnothing$, and $M_{k+1}$ is the pushout of $M_k\leftarrow\coprod_\sigma I(i,-)\otimes\partial\Delta^n\to\coprod_\sigma I(i,-)\otimes\Delta^n$, the coproduct over all squares $\sigma=(i,n,a:\partial\Delta^n\to M_k(i),b:\Delta^n\to E(i))$ with $b|_{\partial\Delta^n}$ equal to $a$ followed by $M_k(i)\to E(i)$; put $M=\operatorname{colim}_kM_k$ with the induced map $M\to E$. Then $\varnothing\to M$ is a $\mathcal J$-cell map, hence lies in ${}^{\pitchfork}(\mathcal J^{\pitchfork})$ by [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization], i.e. $M$ is projectively cofibrant. Colimits are objectwise and $\partial\Delta^n$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices, so every map $\partial\Delta^n\to M(i)$ factors through some $M_k(i)$; the square it belongs to is filled in $M_{k+1}$, so $M\to E$ lies in $\mathcal J^{\pitchfork}$ and is an objectwise trivial Kan fibration. Functoriality: a map of data consists of block-preserving $D\to D'$ and compatible $C_U\to C'_U$, $C_V\to C'_V$, giving $\psi:I\to I'$ and $E\to\psi^*E'$. Inductively define $M_k\to\psi^*M'_k$ over $E\to\psi^*E'$: a square $\sigma$ at $i$ is sent to its image square at $\psi(i)$, and the cell $I(i,-)\otimes K$ maps to $\psi^*(I'(\psi i,-)\otimes K)$ by $\psi$ on mapping sets; $\psi^*$ preserves colimits, so the pushouts and the colimit induce $M\to\psi^*M'$. These maps are defined by the images of squares, hence preserve identities and composites of maps of data, and they need no injectivity of $\psi$ on objects.

source.place: Appendix A.3.3, Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remark A.3.3.5 (projective structure, free cells); explicit countable small-object iteration written here for naturality in the index category.

proof.text: Form $C$ on $U\amalg V$ by retaining $C_U$ and $C_V$ on the diagonal, putting $C(u,v)=M(u,v)$ and $C(v,u)=\varnothing$, and using the two actions for the only mixed compositions $C_V(v,v')\times M(u,v)\times C_U(u',u)\to M(u',v')$. A composable word has at most one mixed arrow, since there are no arrows from $V$ to $U$; the reassociations are the action axioms and their commutation, and the unit laws are the unit axioms. Thus $C$ is a simplicial category, and the identity on objects together with $q_U,q_V$ and $M\to E$ defines a simplicial functor $C\to D$, because $M\to E$ is natural for both actions. A map $M\to\psi^*M'$ of Step 1 likewise extends the given $C_U\to C'_U$, $C_V\to C'_V$ to a functor $C\to C'$ over $D\to D'$, compatibly with composites.

source.place: Appendix A.3.3, Proposition A.3.3.2; direct verification of the collage composition.

proof.text: For an $I$-diagram $N$ write $C(N)$ for the collage of Step 2 built from $N$, so $C=C(M)$. Put $O=U\amalg V$ and $A=C_U\amalg C_V=C(\varnothing)$. For a simplicial category $T$ with object set $O$ and an identity-on-objects functor $s:A\to T$, let $T^s$ be the $I$-diagram $(u,v)\mapsto T(u,v)$ with actions through $s$. A functor $C(N)\to T$ restricting to $s$ is determined by its mixed components $N(u,v)\to T(u,v)$, the reverse mapping sets being empty, and its compatibility with the composites $c_V\circ n\circ c_U$ is exactly naturality for the actions; so $\operatorname{Hom}_{A/\mathrm{sCat}_O}(C(N),T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{sSet}^I}(N,T^s)$, naturally. Hence $N\mapsto C(N)$ is a left adjoint into $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ under $A$ and carries pushouts and countable composites to pushouts and composites in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$. By [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction], $A*F^O_{u_0,v_0}(K)$ represents $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(K,T(u_0,v_0))$ under $A$, as does $C(I((u_0,v_0),-)\otimes K)$ by the adjunction of Step 1; so the collage of a free cell is $A*F^O_{u_0,v_0}(\partial\Delta^n)\to A*F^O_{u_0,v_0}(\Delta^n)$, a pushout of $F^O_{u_0,v_0}(\partial\Delta^n)\to F^O_{u_0,v_0}(\Delta^n)$. The latter has the left lifting property against every local trivial Kan fibration in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$: by the same adjunction a lifting square transposes to a lifting problem of $\partial\Delta^n\to\Delta^n$ against a trivial Kan fibration of mapping sets, solved by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The trivial fibrations of the model structure of [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus] are the local trivial Kan fibrations, so these maps are cofibrations there. Applying $C(-)$ to the filtration of Step 1, $A=C(M_0)\to C(M_1)\to\cdots\to C(M)=C$ is a countable composite of pushouts of coproducts of such maps, hence a cofibration of $\mathrm{sCat}_O$, i.e. a Bergner cofibration by [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus]. In the Bergner structure of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], $A$ is the coproduct of the cofibrant $C_U,C_V$, so $C_U\to A$ and $C_V\to A$ are cofibrations (pushouts of $\varnothing\to C_V$, $\varnothing\to C_U$) and $A$ is cofibrant. Composing, $C$ is Bergner cofibrant and $C_U\to C$, $C_V\to C$ are Bergner cofibrations.

source.place: Bergner, Section 1 generating cofibrations (C1),(C2) (free arrow on a boundary inclusion) and Section 2 Definition 2.1 (free maps); collage left adjoint written here.

proof.text: Evaluation at a fixed $u\in U$, $N\mapsto N(u,-)$, from $I$-diagrams to covariant $C_V$-modules preserves all colimits, since they are objectwise. A free cell at $(u_0,v_0)$ evaluates to $C_V(v_0,-)\otimes(C_U(u,u_0)\times\partial\Delta^n)\to C_V(v_0,-)\otimes(C_U(u,u_0)\times\Delta^n)$, because $I((u_0,v_0),(u,v))=C_U(u,u_0)\times C_V(v_0,v)$. The map of simplicial sets inside is a monomorphism, hence a cofibration by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and the free-module functor $X\mapsto C_V(v_0,-)\otimes X$ preserves cofibrations, being left adjoint to evaluation, which preserves (trivial) fibrations because they are objectwise [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Pushouts, coproducts and countable composites of projective cofibrations are projective cofibrations, so applying evaluation to the filtration of Step 1 shows $M(u,-)$ is projectively cofibrant over $C_V$. Symmetrically, $M(-,v)$ is filtered by cells $C_U(-,u_0)\otimes(C_V(v_0,v)\times\partial\Delta^n)\to C_U(-,u_0)\otimes(C_V(v_0,v)\times\Delta^n)$ and is projectively cofibrant over $C_U^{\mathrm{op}}$. Empty mapping sets give empty cells.

source.place: Appendix A.3.3, Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remark A.3.3.5; restriction of the projective free-cell filtration.

proof.text: On diagonal pairs the map $C\to D$ is $q_U$ or $q_V$, a local trivial fibration by hypothesis; on mixed pairs it is $M(u,v)\to D(u,v)$, a trivial Kan fibration by Step 1; on reverse pairs it is the identity of $\varnothing$, which has the right lifting property against every $\partial\Delta^n\to\Delta^n$ because $\Delta^n$ is nonempty. Therefore $C\to D$ is a local trivial fibration fixing objects. Functoriality was established in Steps 1 and 2. If $U$ or $V$ is empty, $I$ is empty, $M$ is empty and $C$ is $C_V$ or $C_U$; no step uses injectivity of object functions, nonempty blocks or mapping sets, or Kan conditions on $C_U,C_V,D$ (the lifting arguments only use trivial fibrations).

source.place: Appendix A.3.3, Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remark A.3.3.5.

No hypotheses were added; empty blocks and noninjective block maps remain allowed. Reviewer repair (NG maintainer reading, 2026-10-17): Step 1 builds M by an explicit small-object iteration over free cells (cell structure and naturality in the index category made explicit); Step 3 proves the collage is a left adjoint and that free arrow cells are fixed-object cofibrations via the free-arrow adjunction, instead of the unstated converse 'free maps are cofibrations'; Steps 4-5 cite the Kan-Quillen monomorphism/lifting facts.
